name: Tenable Holdings Inc
business: Sells cyber exposure management software (Tenable One, vulnerability management, cloud, identity, OT and AI exposure tools) to enterprises and governments worldwide.

events.what: Interim co-CEOs after CEO Amit Yoran took medical leave
events.who: Stephen A. Vintz (also CFO) and Mark Thurmond (also COO)

events.what: Amit Yoran died; interim co-CEOs continue; Arthur Coviello named Chairman
events.who: Stephen A. Vintz, Mark Thurmond; Arthur W. Coviello Jr. (Chairman)

events.what: Vintz and Thurmond made permanent Co-CEOs (no further CEO change filed through 2026-10-02; Baba roster still lists both as Co-CEO)
New CFO, succeeding Vintz in the CFO role
events.who: Matthew Brown (ex CFO Altair Engineering, interim CFO NortonLifeLock)

next_event.source: Investor Day already held 2026-05-21 (document_id 54669) and set 2029 targets; next is the Q3 2026 earnings call, date not in Baba

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Targets are non-GAAP operating margin (about 28% exiting 2029, about 1.5 points a year from 2025); consensus in Baba is EBITDA. FY2026 consensus EBITDA margin 25.57% vs guided non-GAAP op margin 24.2% gives a 1.37 point D&A-type spread, held flat to restate consensus to the op basis.

statements.quote: Within OpEx, we expect to get about 4 percentage points of leverage spread out across sales and marketing, little tiny bit in R&D, and then some in G&A as well, resulting in operating income, operating margin of about 28%, unlevered free cash flow of 31%. That means we hit rule of 40 exiting 2029.
statements.speaker: Matt Brown

statements.quote: What this ends up translating to is about 1.5 points of operating margin growth each year.
statements.speaker: Matt Brown

statements.quote: For full year 2026, we are raising our guidance range for non-GAAP operating income to $258 million-$264 million or 24.2% of revenue at the midpoint, representing a year-over-year increase of 230 basis points.
statements.speaker: Matt Brown
statements.doc_title: Tenable Holdings Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: December fiscal year, Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years. Compares 28% non-GAAP op margin target (exiting 2029) with FY2029 consensus EBITDA margin 29.86% less a 1.37 point EBITDA-minus-op spread taken from FY2026 (consensus EBITDA margin 25.57% vs guided op margin 24.2%), i.e. street about 28.5% on an op basis.

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 EBITDA margin up 289 bps YoY (VA actuals: 24.9% vs 22.0%); Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating margin 24.7%, up 540 bps YoY (8-K 0001660280-26-000032 EX-99.1, document_id 144178). VA has not yet loaded Q2 2026 EBITDA actual, so LTM EBITDA margin (24.2%) runs 2Q25 to 1Q26.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2029 consensus EBITDA margin 29.86% restates to about 28.5% on an op basis, about 49 bps above the 28% exit-2029 target. Leadership change is internal (co-CEOs were the CFO and COO), and the Investor Day that made the framing numeric has already passed.
verdict: Clean numeric 2029 target and an outside CFO, but the street already models more than the 28% op margin; no unproven gap.
open_questions: Does the co-CEO structure persist, or is a single CEO search pending (nothing filed through 2026-10-02)?
Is the 540 bps Q2 operating margin jump sustainable given planned second-half reinvestment in sales capacity and product?
Does consensus FY2029 revenue (high single digit growth) assume the platform-led growth acceleration management described, which would make the margin path easier?
